learn.hook: Can you count 23 cricket fans without losing track? Tally marks make it easy!
points: A tally mark is one small line for each thing you count.
After 4 standing lines, the 5th line goes across them. That makes a bundle of 5.
To read a tally, count the bundles in 5s: 5, 10, 15 ... then add the single lines.
Tallies help us count things that keep coming, like cars passing by.

example.q: Riya's tally for red cars has 2 bundles of five and 3 single lines. How many red cars did she see?
steps: Now count on the single lines: 11, 12, 13.

learn.reallife: Teachers use tallies to count votes for the class monitor, and scorers use them to count runs in a gully cricket match.

games.title: Match the tally to the number

quiz.q: Arjun's tally has 2 bundles of five and 4 single lines. What number does it show?
quiz.explain: Two bundles of five make 10. Four more lines make 14.
quiz.mistake: Counts each bundle as 1 instead of 5

quiz.q: How many lines are there in one full tally bundle?
quiz.explain: A bundle has 4 standing lines and 1 line across them. That is 5 lines.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count the line that goes across

quiz.q: Meena counted 17 kites. Which tally shows 17?
quiz.explain: 3 bundles of five make 15, and 2 more lines make 17.
quiz.mistake: Thinks each line or bundle stands for the digits of the number

quiz.q: In a class vote, mango got 4 full tally bundles and nothing else. How many votes did mango get?
quiz.explain: Each bundle is 5 votes. Counting in 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20.
quiz.mistake: Counts the bundles but not the lines inside them

quiz.q: Aisha has 9 stickers. How many FULL bundles of five will her tally have?
quiz.explain: 9 is 5 and 4 more. So there is 1 full bundle and 4 single lines.
steps: One bundle of 5, then 4 single lines
quiz.mistake: Rounds 9 up to 10 and thinks there are 2 bundles

quiz.q: Why do we draw the 5th tally line across the other four?
options: It means we must stop counting
It makes groups of 5 so we can count quickly
quiz.explain: Crossing the 5th line makes a neat bundle of 5, so we can count in 5s instead of one by one.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a crossed line means rubbing out

quiz.q: Harpreet's tally of birds has 3 bundles of five and 1 line. Joseph's has 3 bundles of five and 4 lines. How many more birds did Joseph count?
quiz.explain: Harpreet counted 16 and Joseph counted 19. 19 − 16 = 3 more.
quiz.mistake: Gives Joseph's total instead of the difference

quiz.q: A scorer's tally of runs shows 6 full bundles of five. How many runs is that?
quiz.explain: Count in 5s six times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30.
quiz.mistake: Adds 6 and 5 instead of counting six fives

teach.ask: Gappu is counting mangoes with lines and his page is a mess! How do tally marks work?
teach.praise: Wow! Now I can count all the mangoes in fives. Chirp chirp!
teach.nudge: But what do I do when I reach the fifth line?

learn.hook: Your name is full of maths! How many letters does yours have?
points: We can count the letters in a name one by one.
Some names are short, like RIYA (4 letters). Some are long, like HARPREET (8 letters).
A table helps us write down counts neatly.
We can use tally marks to count how many children have names of each length.

example.q: How many letters are in the name JOSEPH?
steps: Point and count: J-1, O-2, S-3, E-4, P-5, H-6.

learn.reallife: When you fill your name in a form, there are boxes for each letter. Counting letters tells you how many boxes you need!

games.title: Name facts
items: RIYA has more letters than KABIR.
RIYA has 4 letters and KABIR has 5.
The letter A comes 2 times in AISHA.
A-I-S-H-A has A at the start and at the end.
MEENA and AISHA have the same number of letters.

quiz.q: How many letters are in the name KABIR?
quiz.explain: K-A-B-I-R. Counting them gives 5 letters.
quiz.mistake: Skips or double-counts a letter

quiz.q: How many letters are in HARPREET?
quiz.explain: H-A-R-P-R-E-E-T has 8 letters. R and E both come twice, so count each one.
quiz.mistake: Counts a repeated letter only once

quiz.q: Which name has the MOST letters?
quiz.explain: JOSEPH has 6 letters. ARJUN has 5, and RIYA and NEHA have 4 each.
quiz.mistake: Picks a name without counting all the letters

quiz.q: How many times does the letter A come in the name AISHA?
quiz.explain: A-I-S-H-A: there is an A at the start and another at the end. That is 2.
steps: Look at each letter: A yes, I no, S no, H no, A yes
quiz.mistake: Only notices the first A

quiz.q: Children in a group: Aisha, Arjun, Riya, Ankit, Meena. How many names start with A?
quiz.explain: Aisha, Arjun and Ankit start with A. Riya and Meena do not. That makes 3.
quiz.mistake: Counts names that have an A anywhere, not just at the start

quiz.q: MEENA has 5 letters. RIYA has 4 letters. How many letters do they have together?
quiz.explain: Put the two counts together: 5 + 4 = 9 letters.
quiz.mistake: Finds the difference instead of the total

quiz.q: A class table says: 6 children have 4-letter names, 9 have 5-letter names and 4 have 6-letter names. Which name length is most common?
quiz.explain: 9 is the biggest count, so 5-letter names are the most common.
quiz.mistake: Picks the biggest name length (6) instead of the biggest count

quiz.q: Using the same table (6, 9 and 4 children), how many children are in the class?
quiz.explain: Add all the counts: 6 + 9 + 4 = 19 children.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the three groups

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know which friend has the longest name. How can he find out?
teach.praise: Yay! I counted all the letters and found the longest name!
teach.nudge: How do I know which name is the longest? What should I compare?

learn.hook: Who has more laddoos, you or your cousin? Maths can settle it fairly!
points: To compare, we find out which group is more, which is fewer, or if they are the same.
Line up two groups one-to-one. Things left over show which group has more.
To find HOW MANY more, take the smaller number away from the bigger one.
We can also count on from the smaller number to the bigger number.

example.q: Kabir has 12 marbles. Meena has 8 marbles. How many more marbles does Kabir have?
steps: The bigger number is 12, the smaller is 8.
Count on from 8 to 12: 9, 10, 11, 12. That is 4 steps.

learn.reallife: At a market, you compare prices to see which shop is cheaper, and in cricket you compare scores to see who won.

games.title: Line up the scores
games.prompt: Arrange the runs from fewest to most

quiz.q: Riya has 14 bangles. Aisha has 9 bangles. How many more bangles does Riya have?
quiz.explain: Take the smaller number from the bigger one: 14 − 9 = 5.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Which box has the FEWEST crayons?
quiz.explain: 18 is the smallest of 18, 24, 31 and 20, so that box has the fewest crayons.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up fewer with more

quiz.q: Arjun scored 25 runs and Kabir scored 32 runs. How many more runs did Kabir score?
quiz.explain: 32 − 25 = 7. Count on from 25: 26 ... 30 is 5, then 31, 32 is 2 more. 5 + 2 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Counts one step too many when counting on

quiz.q: Meena has 16 stickers. Joseph has 16 stickers too. What is true?
quiz.explain: Both have 16, so neither has more. They have the same number.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one person must always have more

quiz.q: Harpreet has 10 diyas. She needs 18 diyas for Diwali. How many more diyas does she need?
quiz.explain: From 10 to 18 is 8 more. So 18 − 10 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 and 18 instead of finding what is missing

quiz.q: A basket has 21 bananas and another has 12 bananas. Which is correct?
quiz.explain: 21 has 2 tens and 12 has only 1 ten, so 21 is more.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit (1 and 2) instead of the tens

quiz.q: Aisha has 6 fewer pencils than Riya. Riya has 15 pencils. How many does Aisha have?
quiz.explain: Fewer means take away: 15 − 6 = 9 pencils.
quiz.mistake: Adds when the word 'fewer' means take away

quiz.q: Kabir has 4 more toy cars than Arjun. Arjun has 11. How many toy cars does Kabir have?
quiz.explain: 4 more than 11 is 11 + 4 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Takes away when the question says 'more'

teach.ask: Gappu has 7 worms and his sister has 10. He wants to know how many more she has. Can you help?
teach.praise: Now I know she has 3 more worms. I will ask her to share!
teach.nudge: I know she has more. But how do I find HOW MANY more?

learn.hook: Your toy box is full of secret shapes! A ball, a dice and a party cap are all maths shapes.
points: Solid things that we can hold are 3D shapes.
A ball or a laddoo is a sphere. A dice is a cube.
A brick or a matchbox is a cuboid. A round candle is a cylinder.
A birthday cap or an ice-cream cone is a cone.

example.q: Aisha's toy rocket has a pointed top and a long round body. Which shapes are these?
steps: The pointed top is like a birthday cap, so it is a cone.
The long round body with flat round ends is a cylinder.
example.answer: A cone on top of a cylinder

learn.reallife: Look around the kitchen: a laddoo is a sphere, a matchbox is a cuboid and a steel dabba with a round lid is often a cylinder.

games.title: Match the toy to its shape

quiz.q: A cricket ball is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A ball is round all over with no flat part. That shape is a sphere.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a sphere with a cylinder because both are round

quiz.q: Which shape is a ludo dice?
quiz.explain: A dice has 6 square faces that are all the same size. That is a cube.
quiz.mistake: Calls every box shape a cuboid without checking if all faces are squares

quiz.q: A round candle stands on a flat round end. What shape is it?
quiz.explain: It has two flat round ends and a curved side, just like a cylinder.
quiz.mistake: Thinks anything round must be a sphere

quiz.q: A birthday party cap is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: It has one round edge at the bottom and a pointed tip at the top. That is a cone.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a cone and a cylinder

quiz.q: Which of these is shaped like a cuboid?
quiz.explain: A brick is a box shape with 6 flat rectangle faces. That is a cuboid.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name for a box shape

quiz.q: Which object is NOT shaped like a sphere?
quiz.explain: A dice has flat square faces and corners, so it is a cube, not a sphere.
quiz.mistake: Misses the word NOT in the question

quiz.q: Meena's toy rocket has a cone on top of a cylinder. Which part is the pointed top?
quiz.explain: A cone has a pointed tip, so the pointed top is the cone.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder can have a pointed end

quiz.q: How many of these are spheres: a ball, a marble, a brick, a globe?
quiz.explain: The ball, the marble and the globe are round all over. The brick is a cuboid. So 3 are spheres.
quiz.mistake: Counts the brick too

teach.ask: Gappu found a ball, a dice and a party cap. He thinks they are all the same shape! Can you tell him their names?
teach.praise: Sphere, cube, cone! Now I know my toy shapes!
teach.nudge: What is the name of the pointed party cap shape?

learn.hook: Run your finger over a dice. Flat parts, sharp lines, pointy tips - each one has a name!
points: A face is a flat surface of a solid shape.
An edge is a line where two faces meet.
A corner is a point where edges meet.
A cube and a cuboid each have 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 corners.
A sphere has no flat face, no edge and no corner.

example.q: How many faces does a matchbox (a cuboid) have?

learn.reallife: When you wrap a gift box for Raksha Bandhan, you cover all 6 faces of the box with paper.

games.title: Shape detective
items: A cube has top, bottom, front, back, left and right: 6 square faces.
A sphere is round all over. It has no corners at all.
An edge is where two faces meet.
The line where two flat faces join is called an edge.
A cylinder has a flat circle at the top and one at the bottom.
A cone has just 1 pointed tip.
Like a cube, a cuboid has 4 corners on top and 4 at the bottom.

quiz.q: How many faces does a cube have?
quiz.explain: Top, bottom, front, back, left and right: a cube has 6 square faces.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the faces that can be seen at one time

quiz.q: How many corners does a cube have?
quiz.explain: A cube has 4 corners on the top and 4 corners on the bottom. 4 + 4 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up corners with faces

quiz.q: How many edges does a cube have?
quiz.explain: 4 edges go round the top, 4 go round the bottom and 4 stand up at the sides. 4 + 4 + 4 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up edges with corners

quiz.q: How many flat faces does a cylinder have?
quiz.explain: A cylinder has a flat circle on top and a flat circle at the bottom. Its side is curved, not flat.
quiz.mistake: Counts the curved side as a flat face

quiz.q: Which shape has no flat face, no edge and no corner?
quiz.explain: A sphere is round all over, like a ball. It has nothing flat, no edge and no corner.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder has no faces because it is round

quiz.q: How many pointed corners does a cone have?
quiz.explain: A cone has only one pointed tip at the top.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the round bottom edge has corners

quiz.q: A matchbox is a cuboid. How many faces does it have?
quiz.explain: A cuboid, like a cube, has 6 faces: top, bottom, front, back and two sides.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the bottom face that sits on the table

quiz.q: Riya traces round the flat face of a cylinder on paper. What shape does she draw?
quiz.explain: The flat faces of a cylinder are round, so the tracing is a circle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of the side view of the cylinder instead of its flat face

teach.ask: Gappu is holding a dice. He asks: what are faces, edges and corners?
teach.praise: Flat faces, straight edges, pointy corners! My dice makes sense now!
teach.nudge: Which part of the dice is the corner? And what is an edge?

learn.hook: Why does a ball run away but a dice stays put? Let's find out!
points: Shapes with a curved surface can roll. A sphere rolls in every direction.
Shapes with a flat face can slide. A cube and a cuboid slide but do not roll.
A cylinder and a cone can roll and can also slide on a flat face.
Shapes with flat faces are easy to stack, so cubes make strong towers.

example.q: Kabir wants to build the tallest tower. Should he use balls or dice?
steps: Balls have no flat face, so they roll off each other.
Dice have flat faces, so one sits firmly on another.
example.answer: Dice, because flat faces stack well.

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers stack cuboid boxes on shelves, but they keep oranges in baskets so they do not roll away.

items.text: A dice can ___ but not roll.
A shape needs a ___ face to slide.
A shape needs a ___ surface to roll.

quiz.q: Which shape can only roll and cannot slide on its face?
quiz.explain: A sphere has no flat face at all, so it can only roll.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a cylinder can only roll and forgets its flat faces

quiz.q: Which shape slides but does not roll?
quiz.explain: A cube has only flat faces and no curved surface, so it slides but cannot roll.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any shape can roll if you push it hard

quiz.q: What can a cylinder do on a flat floor?
quiz.explain: On its curved side a cylinder rolls. Standing on a flat face, it slides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks of only one way the cylinder can lie

quiz.q: Which toys are easiest to stack into a tall tower?
quiz.explain: Cubes have flat faces on every side, so each one sits firmly on the one below.
quiz.mistake: Does not think about whether faces are flat

quiz.q: Why can a tin can roll?
quiz.explain: Things roll on curved surfaces. A tin can's side is curved, so it rolls.
quiz.mistake: Thinks weight makes things roll

quiz.q: Kabir stands a cone on its pointed tip at the bottom of a tower. What happens?
options: The cone turns into a cube
quiz.explain: A tip is just a point, so the cone cannot balance on it. The tower topples.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any face or tip can hold up a tower

quiz.q: A toy train has 4 coaches. Each coach has 4 round wheels. How many wheels do the coaches have?
quiz.explain: 4 coaches with 4 wheels each: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 16 wheels.
quiz.mistake: Adds only 4 + 4 for the coaches and wheels

quiz.q: A clown toy has a sphere head, a cylinder body and a cone hat. How many DIFFERENT shapes are used?
quiz.explain: Sphere, cylinder and cone are three different shapes.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to count one of the parts

teach.ask: Gappu's ball keeps rolling away but his dice stays still. Why?
teach.praise: Curved things roll, flat things slide! I will stack my dice now.
teach.nudge: What is different about the ball's surface and the dice's faces?

learn.hook: A batter who scores 200 runs hits a double century! Let's count all the way there.
points: After 100 we keep counting: 101, 102, 103 ... just like 1, 2, 3 with a 1 in front.
After 109 comes 110, and after 199 comes 200.
Counting by 10s is quick: 100, 110, 120, 130 ...
The number just after is 1 more. The number just before is 1 less.

example.q: What comes just after 159, and just before 160?
steps: 1 more than 159: the ones go from 9 to 10, so we get 160.

learn.reallife: Cricket scoreboards, page numbers in a big storybook and seat numbers on a train all go past 100.

games.title: Climb to 200
games.prompt: Put the numbers from smallest to biggest

quiz.q: What number comes just after 199?
quiz.explain: 1 more than 199 is 200. The 9 tens and 9 ones become 1 more hundred.
quiz.mistake: Writes 1100 by putting 1 and 100 side by side

quiz.q: What number comes just before 150?
quiz.explain: Just before means 1 less. 150 − 1 = 149.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number just after instead of just before

quiz.q: Count on by tens: 120, 130, 140, ___
quiz.explain: Each step adds 10. 140 + 10 = 150.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: Which number comes between 178 and 180?
quiz.explain: 178, 179, 180. The number in the middle is 179.
quiz.mistake: Picks a number next to only one of them

quiz.q: Riya's train seat number is 1 more than 109. What is her seat number?
quiz.explain: 1 more than 109 is 110. The ones go from 9 to 10, making one more ten.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 instead of 1

quiz.q: Count back by tens: 200, 190, 180, ___
quiz.explain: Counting back by 10 takes away 10 each time. 180 − 10 = 170.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: Arjun's mother made 100 laddoos, and then 25 more. How many laddoos in all?
quiz.explain: 100 and 25 more make 125.
quiz.mistake: Writes 100 and 25 side by side as 1025

quiz.q: Skip count by fives: 185, 190, 195, ___
quiz.explain: Each step adds 5. 195 + 5 = 200.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 5

teach.ask: Gappu counted 197, 198, 199... and got stuck! What comes next, and why?
teach.praise: Two hundred! A double century! Thank you!
teach.nudge: What happens when I add one more to 199?

learn.hook: Ten sticks make a bundle, and ten bundles make a giant bundle. That giant bundle is 100!
points: 10 ones make 1 ten. 10 tens make 1 hundred.
In 147, the 1 means 1 hundred, the 4 means 4 tens and the 7 means 7 ones.
The value of a digit depends on its place. The 4 in 147 is worth 40.
If a place is empty, we write 0 there, like 203 = 2 hundreds, 0 tens, 3 ones.

example.q: Kabir has 1 bundle of 100 sticks, 6 bundles of 10 and 5 loose sticks. How many sticks?

learn.reallife: Money works like this too: ₹100 notes are hundreds, ₹10 notes are tens and ₹1 coins are ones.

quiz.q: 1 hundred, 4 tens and 7 ones make which number?
quiz.explain: Hundreds first, then tens, then ones: 100 + 40 + 7 = 147.
quiz.mistake: Adds the digits 1 + 4 + 7 instead of using place value

quiz.q: How many tens make 1 hundred?
quiz.mistake: Thinks a hundred is made of 100 tens

quiz.q: In 186, what is the value of the digit 8?
quiz.explain: 8 is in the tens place, so it means 8 tens = 80.
quiz.mistake: Gives the digit instead of its value

quiz.q: Kabir has 2 bundles of 100 sticks and 3 loose sticks. How many sticks does he have?
quiz.explain: 2 hundreds and 3 ones with no tens: 200 + 0 + 3 = 203. The 0 keeps the tens place.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to put 0 in the empty tens place

quiz.q: How many tens are there in 160 altogether?
quiz.explain: 1 hundred is 10 tens. Add the 6 tens to get 16 tens.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the tens digit

quiz.q: What is the hundreds digit in 215?
quiz.explain: In 215, the first digit 2 is in the hundreds place.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the hundreds place with the tens or ones place

quiz.q: Which one shows 172?
quiz.explain: 172 = 100 + 70 + 2, so it is 1 hundred, 7 tens and 2 ones.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the tens and ones digits

quiz.q: Meena has one ₹100 note, five ₹10 notes and three ₹1 coins. How much money does she have?
quiz.mistake: Counts the number of notes and coins instead of their value

teach.ask: Gappu sees the number 147 and thinks it just means 1, 4 and 7. Can you explain what each digit means?
teach.praise: 1 hundred, 4 tens and 7 ones! Every digit has its own home.
teach.nudge: But what is the 4 really worth in 147?

learn.hook: Which is more, 189 or 198? The digits are the same, but one number is bigger!
points: To compare, look at the hundreds first. More hundreds means a bigger number.
If the hundreds are the same, compare the tens. If the tens are the same, compare the ones.
We use > for 'greater than', < for 'less than' and = for 'equal to'.
We read 163 as 'one hundred sixty-three'.

example.q: Compare 189 and 198.
steps: Tens: 8 tens and 9 tens. 9 tens is more.

learn.reallife: When two shops sell the same toy, you compare the prices to pick the cheaper one.

games.title: Biggest first
games.prompt: Put the numbers from biggest to smallest

games.title: Greater or less?
items: Both have 1 hundred. 7 tens is more than 6 tens.
201 has 2 hundreds and 199 has only 1, so 201 is greater.
Both have 1 hundred. 3 tens is more than 0 tens.
One hundred four is 104: 1 hundred, 0 tens, 4 ones.

quiz.q: Which is greater: 189 or 198?
quiz.explain: Both have 1 hundred. 198 has 9 tens and 189 has 8 tens, so 198 is greater.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the ones digit (9 is bigger than 8) instead of the tens

quiz.q: How do we write 140 in words?
quiz.explain: 140 is 1 hundred and 4 tens, so we say one hundred forty.
quiz.mistake: Drops the zero and reads 140 like 14

quiz.q: Which is the smallest number: 205, 150, 199, 120?
quiz.explain: 205 has 2 hundreds, so it is biggest. The others have 1 hundred; compare tens: 2 tens is the least, so 120 is smallest.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the last digit to decide

quiz.q: Write 'one hundred sixty-three' in numbers.
quiz.explain: One hundred is 100, sixty is 60, three is 3. 100 + 60 + 3 = 163.
quiz.mistake: Writes each word's number side by side, like 100 then 63

quiz.q: Which sign makes this true? 176 ___ 167
quiz.explain: Both have 1 hundred. 7 tens is more than 6 tens, so 176 is greater: 176 > 167.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the > and < signs

quiz.q: Joseph's school has 212 children. Aisha's school has 221 children. Which school has more children?
quiz.explain: Both have 2 hundreds. 221 has 2 tens and 212 has 1 ten, so Aisha's school has more.
quiz.mistake: Compares the ones digits first

quiz.q: Which is the largest number: 199, 201, 120, 210?
quiz.explain: 201 and 210 have 2 hundreds. Then compare tens: 1 ten beats 0 tens, so 210 is largest.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 199 is biggest because it has many 9s

quiz.q: Using the digits 2, 0 and 1 once each, what is the smallest 3-digit number you can make?
quiz.explain: A 3-digit number cannot start with 0. Put the smallest non-zero digit, 1, first, then 0, then 2: 102.
quiz.mistake: Puts 0 in the hundreds place, which makes only a 2-digit number

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 189 is bigger than 198 because 9 is at the end. Is he right? Explain to him.
teach.praise: Check hundreds first, then tens! Now I won't get fooled.
teach.nudge: Which place should I look at first when comparing?

learn.hook: Riya is going to Nani Maa's village by train! Let's add up all the fun things on the trip.
points: Adding means putting things together to find the total.
Words like 'in all', 'altogether' and 'total' tell us to add.
Add the tens, then the ones: for 34 + 25, do 30 + 20 = 50 and 4 + 5 = 9. So 34 + 25 = 59.
If the ones make 10 or more, they make a new ten. Add it to the tens.

example.q: Nani Maa picked 26 mangoes on Monday and 18 mangoes on Tuesday. How many mangoes in all?

learn.reallife: On a trip we add up tickets, snacks and even the cows we spot from the train window!

items.text: Riya had 12 shells and found ___ more. Now she has 20.

quiz.q: From the train window, Arjun counted 34 cows and then 23 goats. How many animals did he count in all?
quiz.explain: 'In all' means add. 34 + 23 = 57.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of adding

quiz.q: Nani Maa made 45 laddoos and 28 jalebis. How many sweets did she make altogether?
quiz.explain: 5 + 8 = 13 makes a new ten. 60 + 13 = 73.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the new ten made by 5 + 8 = 13

quiz.q: Riya's train ticket cost ₹65 and her brother's ticket also cost ₹65. What was the total cost?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the 10 made by 5 + 5

quiz.q: At Nani Maa's farm there are 16 hens and 7 ducks. How many birds are there in all?
quiz.explain: 16 + 7: first 16 + 4 = 20, then 3 more makes 23.
quiz.mistake: Counts on but misses one step

quiz.q: Which words in a story tell you to ADD?
quiz.explain: 'In all' means put everything together, so we add. The others mean something was taken away.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up adding words with taking-away words

quiz.q: Meena walked 38 steps to the well and 38 steps back. How many steps did she walk?
quiz.mistake: Forgets the new ten made by 8 + 8 = 16

quiz.q: Joseph has 50 marbles. Nani Maa gives him 25 more. How many marbles does he have now?
quiz.explain: He gets more, so we add. 50 + 25 = 75.
quiz.mistake: Takes away when the story says he got more

quiz.q: Riya packed 14 frocks, 6 T-shirts and 10 pairs of socks. How many things did she pack?
quiz.explain: Add all three: 14 + 6 = 20, and 20 + 10 = 30.
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the three groups

teach.ask: Gappu has 25 berries and finds 13 more. He wants to know how many he has now. How should he work it out?
teach.praise: Tens with tens, ones with ones! I have 38 berries. Yum!
teach.nudge: Should I add or take away? And which parts do I add first?

learn.hook: Nani Maa had a big basket of mangoes, but the monkeys came visiting! How many are left?
points: Subtracting means taking away to find what is left.
Words like 'left', 'gave away', 'how many more' and 'difference' tell us to subtract.
Take away tens, then ones: for 58 − 23, do 50 − 20 = 30 and 8 − 3 = 5. So 58 − 23 = 35.
If there are not enough ones, break a ten into 10 ones.
Check by adding back: 35 + 23 = 58.

example.q: Nani Maa had 52 mangoes. The monkeys took 17. How many mangoes are left?

learn.reallife: When you spend some of your pocket money at the village fair, subtraction tells you how much is left.

games.title: True or false?
items: 4 tens − 2 tens = 2 tens, and the 8 ones stay. That is 28.
Taking away makes a number smaller. 60 − 5 = 55.
Take everything away and nothing is left.
'How many are left?' tells us to add.
'Left' means some were taken away, so we subtract.

quiz.q: Arjun took 40 photos on the trip. He deleted 15 blurry ones. How many photos are left?
quiz.explain: 'Left' means take away. 40 − 15 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away

quiz.q: The train coach had 86 seats. 54 people sat down. How many seats are empty?
quiz.explain: Take the filled seats away from all the seats: 86 − 54 = 32.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers

quiz.q: Nani Maa had 30 cups of milk. She used 12 cups to make kheer. How many cups are left?
quiz.explain: 30 − 12: take away 10 to get 20, then take away 2 more to get 18.
quiz.mistake: Does 2 − 0 instead of 0 − 2 in the ones place and gets 22

quiz.q: Kabir is 9 years old and Nani Maa is 64 years old. How much older is Nani Maa?
quiz.explain: 'How much older' asks for the difference. 64 − 9 = 55.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two ages instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Riya has 25 bangles. She wants 40 bangles for a wedding. How many more bangles does she need?
quiz.explain: Count on from 25 to 40: that is 15. So 40 − 25 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 25 and 40 instead of finding what is missing

quiz.q: Meena had ₹70. She bought a kite for ₹35. How much money does she have left?
quiz.explain: 70 − 35: take away 30 to get 40, then take away 5 to get 35.
quiz.mistake: Adds the price instead of taking it away

quiz.q: Which addition checks that 62 − 27 = 35 is correct?
quiz.explain: Add the answer to the number taken away. If you get back 62, the subtraction is right. 35 + 27 = 62.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers from the question instead of the answer and the number taken away

quiz.q: There were 48 chickens in the yard. 19 went into the coop. How many are still outside?
quiz.explain: 48 − 19: take away 10 to get 38, then take away 9 to get 29.
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller ones digit from the bigger one (9 − 8 = 1) and gets 31

teach.ask: Gappu had 32 seeds and ate 15. He wants to know how many are left but doesn't know where to start. Help him!
teach.praise: I break a ten when I need more ones! I have 17 seeds left. Chirp!
teach.nudge: But 2 is smaller than 5. What can I do with the ones?

learn.hook: Can you add 39 + 26 in your head, with no paper? Here are some magic tricks!
points: To add 9, add 10 and take away 1: 46 + 9 = 56 − 1 = 55.
Add tens by jumping: 43 + 30 = 73, just 3 jumps of ten.

example.q: Find 58 + 9 in your head.

learn.reallife: At the sabzi market, you can add prices in your head and know the total before the shopkeeper tells you!

quiz.q: What is 47 + 9? Try this: add 10, then take away 1.
quiz.explain: 47 + 10 = 57. We added 1 too many, so 57 − 1 = 56.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 but forgets to take away the extra 1

quiz.q: Nani Maa gave 20 sweets to Riya and 20 sweets to Arjun. How many sweets did she give in all?
quiz.explain: 2 tens and 2 tens make 4 tens. 20 + 20 = 40.
quiz.mistake: Counts only one child's sweets

quiz.q: Double 15 is 30. So what is 15 + 16?
quiz.explain: 16 is one more than 15, so 15 + 16 is one more than 30. That is 31.
quiz.mistake: Gives the double without adding the extra 1

quiz.q: Which way gives the correct answer to 29 + 14?
quiz.explain: 29 is 1 less than 30. So 30 + 14 = 44, then take away 1 to get 43.
quiz.mistake: Rounds 29 up to 30 but then adds the extra 1 instead of taking it away

quiz.q: Kabir had 63 stamps. His uncle gave him 30 more. How many stamps does he have now?
quiz.explain: Adding 30 means jumping 3 tens: 63, 73, 83, 93.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 ones instead of 3 tens

quiz.q: What is 8 + 6? Make a ten first: 8 + 2 + 4.
quiz.explain: 8 + 2 makes 10. Then 4 more makes 14.
quiz.mistake: Loses count when breaking 6 into 2 and 4

quiz.q: What is 70 − 30?
quiz.explain: 7 tens take away 3 tens leaves 4 tens. That is 40.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting

quiz.q: Harpreet bought a book for ₹49 and a pen for ₹20. Think ₹50 + ₹20 − ₹1. What is the total?
quiz.explain: ₹50 + ₹20 = ₹70. The book was ₹1 less than ₹50, so take away 1: ₹69.
quiz.mistake: Rounds up to 50 but forgets to take away the extra 1

teach.ask: Gappu wants to add 39 + 15 in his head but has no paper. Teach him a trick!
teach.praise: 40 + 15 = 55, take away 1 is 54! I am a mental maths bird now!
teach.nudge: If I make 39 into 40, what must I do at the end?

learn.hook: Look at a roti, a samosa and a carrom board. Each one is hiding a flat shape!
points: Flat shapes that we can draw on paper are called 2D shapes.
A circle is perfectly round, like a roti or a bangle.
A triangle has 3 straight sides, like the front of a samosa.
A square has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners. A rectangle has 4 square corners, with 2 long sides and 2 short sides.
The flat faces of solid shapes are 2D shapes: each face of a dice is a square.

example.q: Name the shape of a ₹5 coin, a carrom board and a door.
steps: The coin is round all the way: a circle.
The carrom board has 4 equal sides: a square.
The door has 2 long sides and 2 short sides: a rectangle.

learn.reallife: Rangoli designs, windows, kites, tiles and chapatis are all full of 2D shapes.

games.title: Match the thing to its shape

quiz.q: A roti is shaped like a ___.
quiz.explain: A roti is round all the way around, with no corners. That is a circle.
quiz.mistake: Does not know the name of the round shape

quiz.q: Which shape has 3 straight sides?
quiz.explain: 'Tri' means three. A triangle has 3 straight sides.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up a triangle with a 4-sided shape

quiz.q: A carrom board has 4 equal sides and 4 square corners. What shape is it?
quiz.explain: 4 equal sides with square corners make a square.
quiz.mistake: Does not count the sides before naming the shape

quiz.q: A door has 2 long sides, 2 short sides and 4 square corners. What shape is it?
quiz.explain: A shape with 4 square corners and 2 long and 2 short sides is a rectangle.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every 4-sided shape is a square

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a flat (2D) shape?
quiz.explain: A cube is a solid shape you can hold, like a dice. The others are flat shapes.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up flat shapes with solid shapes

quiz.q: Aisha puts a dice on paper and draws around one face. What shape does she get?
quiz.explain: Every face of a dice is a square, so the drawing is a square.
quiz.mistake: Names the solid shape instead of the shape of its face

quiz.q: Each cell of a honeycomb has 6 sides. What is a 6-sided shape called?
quiz.explain: A shape with 6 sides is a hexagon. A pentagon has 5 sides.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up hexagon (6 sides) and pentagon (5 sides)

quiz.q: Which shape has no corners at all?
quiz.explain: A circle is one smooth curved line, so it has no corners.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice that the other shapes have corners

teach.ask: Gappu thinks a door and a carrom board are the same shape. Can you tell him the difference?
teach.praise: The carrom board is a square and the door is a rectangle! Now I see it.
teach.nudge: Are all the sides of a door the same length?

learn.hook: Count the corners of your notebook. You can name many shapes just by counting!
points: A side is a straight line along the edge of a flat shape.
A corner is where two sides meet.
A triangle has 3 sides and 3 corners. A square and a rectangle have 4 sides and 4 corners.
A pentagon has 5 sides and 5 corners. A hexagon has 6 sides and 6 corners.
A circle has no straight sides and no corners.

example.q: How many sides do 2 triangles and 1 square have altogether?

learn.reallife: When you make shapes with matchsticks or ice-cream sticks, each stick is one side.

quiz.q: How many corners does a triangle have?
quiz.explain: A triangle has 3 sides, and they meet at 3 corners.
quiz.mistake: Guesses without counting the corners

quiz.q: How many sides does a pentagon have?
quiz.explain: A pentagon has 5 sides, like the outline of a simple house drawing.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up pentagon and hexagon

quiz.q: Which shape has 6 sides and 6 corners?
quiz.explain: A hexagon has 6 sides and 6 corners.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a pentagon has 6 sides

quiz.q: Joseph made a shape with 4 matchsticks of the same length and 4 square corners. What shape did he make?
quiz.explain: 4 equal sides with square corners make a square.
quiz.mistake: Does not match the number of sticks to the number of sides

quiz.q: Riya makes 3 separate triangles with sticks, one stick for each side. How many sticks does she need?
quiz.explain: Each triangle needs 3 sticks. 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 sticks.
quiz.mistake: Counts the triangles instead of their sides

quiz.q: How many corners does a circle have?
quiz.explain: A circle has no straight sides, so no sides meet to make a corner. It has 0 corners.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the round edge has a corner somewhere

quiz.q: Meena counts the corners of a square and a triangle together. How many corners does she count?
quiz.explain: A square has 4 corners and a triangle has 3. 4 + 3 = 7.
quiz.mistake: Thinks a triangle has 4 corners too

quiz.q: A shape with straight sides has 5 corners. How many sides does it have?
quiz.explain: In a shape with straight sides, the number of sides is the same as the number of corners. So it has 5 sides.
quiz.mistake: Thinks sides and corners must be different numbers

teach.ask: Gappu drew a shape and wants to know its name. What should he count?
teach.praise: 3 sides and 3 corners, it's a triangle! Counting is magic!
teach.nudge: What two things can I count on my shape?

learn.hook: Seven pieces, one square, endless pictures! A tangram can become a cat, a boat or a rocket.
points: A tangram is a square puzzle cut into 7 pieces.
It has 5 triangles, 1 square and 1 slanting 4-sided piece called a parallelogram.
The triangles come in sizes: 2 big, 1 middle-sized and 2 small.
Two small triangles can be joined to make the square piece.
We put the pieces side by side, without overlapping, to make animals, people and things.

example.q: How many of the 7 tangram pieces are NOT triangles?
steps: They are the square and the parallelogram.

learn.reallife: Tangrams are a puzzle game from long ago. You can cut one from a square of paper and play with your friends.

games.title: Tangram facts
items: 5 are triangles, but there is also a square and a parallelogram.
Two small triangles can make a square.
Put their long sides together and you get a square.
It has 2 big triangles, 1 middle-sized one and 2 small ones.
The pieces lie flat side by side without covering each other.
Two small triangles can join to make a bigger triangle.
Join them along a short side and they make the middle-sized triangle.

items.text: The only piece with 4 equal sides is the ___.

quiz.q: How many pieces are there in a tangram?
quiz.explain: A tangram has 7 pieces: 5 triangles, 1 square and 1 parallelogram.
quiz.mistake: Counts only the triangles

quiz.q: How many of the tangram pieces are triangles?
quiz.explain: 2 big + 1 middle + 2 small = 5 triangles.
quiz.mistake: Counts all 7 pieces as triangles

quiz.q: Which shape can you make by joining the long sides of the 2 small tangram triangles?
quiz.explain: Two small triangles joined along their long sides make a square, the same size as the square piece.
quiz.mistake: Thinks joining triangles always makes a bigger triangle

quiz.q: Kabir makes a boat using 3 triangles and 1 square. How many corners do these pieces have altogether?
quiz.explain: 3 triangles have 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 corners. The square has 4. 9 + 4 = 13.
quiz.mistake: Counts 4 corners for every piece

quiz.q: Which tangram piece is NOT a triangle and NOT a square?
quiz.explain: The parallelogram is the slanting 4-sided piece. It is not a triangle or a square.
quiz.mistake: Forgets that a tangram has a slanting piece

quiz.q: Aisha used all 7 pieces to make a cat. 5 of them were triangles. How many other pieces did she use?
quiz.explain: 7 pieces in all, 5 triangles. 7 − 5 = 2 other pieces: the square and the parallelogram.
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 and 5 instead of taking away

quiz.q: When we make a tangram picture, the pieces must ___.
quiz.explain: Tangram pieces lie flat, side by side, without covering one another.
quiz.mistake: Thinks pieces can be stacked on top of each other

quiz.q: How many big triangles are there in a tangram?
quiz.explain: A tangram has 2 big triangles, 1 middle-sized triangle and 2 small triangles.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the number of big and small triangles

teach.ask: Gappu has 7 tangram pieces but doesn't know what they are. Tell him!
teach.praise: 5 triangles, a square and a parallelogram! I made a bird with them!
teach.nudge: Are all the pieces triangles? What other shapes are there?

learn.hook: A cinema hall can have hundreds of seats! Let's learn to read and write such big numbers.
points: We can count in hundreds: 100, 200, 300 ... up to 900.
A 3-digit number has a hundreds digit, a tens digit and a ones digit.
We read 457 as 'four hundred fifty-seven'.
The smallest 3-digit number is 100 and the largest is 999.
After 999 comes 1000, our first 4-digit number.

example.q: Write 'six hundred eight' in numbers.
steps: No tens, so the tens digit is 0

learn.reallife: Bus numbers, house numbers and the price of a school bag often have 3 digits.

items.text: Eight hundred twenty in numbers is ___.

quiz.q: Count in hundreds: 200, 300, 400, ___
quiz.explain: Each step adds 1 hundred. 400 + 100 = 500.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 100

quiz.q: Write 'five hundred thirty-six' in numbers.
quiz.explain: Five hundred is 500, thirty is 30 and six is 6. 500 + 30 + 6 = 536.
quiz.mistake: Writes 500 and then 36 next to it

quiz.q: Write 'seven hundred four' in numbers.
quiz.explain: 7 hundreds, no tens and 4 ones. The 0 holds the tens place: 704.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 0 in the tens place

quiz.q: What number comes just after 599?
quiz.explain: 1 more than 599 is 600. The 9 ones and 9 tens roll over into one more hundred.
quiz.mistake: Writes 5 and then 100 next to it

quiz.q: Which is the largest 3-digit number?
quiz.explain: 999 has the biggest digit, 9, in every place. 1000 has 4 digits.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1000 is a 3-digit number

quiz.q: How do you read 860?
quiz.explain: 860 is 8 hundreds and 6 tens, so we say eight hundred sixty.
quiz.mistake: Ignores the 0 or reads the digits in the wrong places

quiz.q: A cinema has 300 seats downstairs and 200 seats upstairs. How many seats are there in all?
quiz.explain: 3 hundreds and 2 hundreds make 5 hundreds. 300 + 200 = 500.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of adding

quiz.q: Count back in hundreds: 900, 800, 700, ___
quiz.explain: Each step takes away 1 hundred. 700 − 100 = 600.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 1 instead of 100

teach.ask: Gappu sees 'five hundred forty-two' on a bus. How should he write it in numbers?
teach.praise: 542! Five hundreds, four tens and two ones. I can read buses now!
teach.nudge: Which digit goes first, and what does 'forty' become?

learn.hook: Every digit lives in its own house: Hundreds House, Tens House or Ones House!
points: In 358, the 3 is in the hundreds place, the 5 is in the tens place and the 8 is in the ones place.
358 = 300 + 50 + 8. This is called the expanded form.
The same digit has a different value in a different place. In 535, the first 5 is worth 500 and the last 5 is worth 5.
Zero keeps a place empty: 405 has 0 tens.

example.q: Write 642 in expanded form.

learn.reallife: ₹100 notes, ₹10 notes and ₹1 coins work just like hundreds, tens and ones.

quiz.q: What is the value of the digit 7 in 739?
quiz.explain: 7 is in the hundreds place, so it is worth 7 hundreds = 700.
quiz.mistake: Gives the digit instead of its value

quiz.q: Which is the expanded form of 481?
quiz.explain: 4 hundreds, 8 tens and 1 one: 400 + 80 + 1.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits without their place values

quiz.q: 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 9 ones make which number?
quiz.explain: 400 + 0 + 9 = 409. The 0 keeps the tens place.
quiz.mistake: Leaves out the 0 in the tens place

quiz.q: Harpreet has three ₹100 notes, two ₹10 notes and six ₹1 coins. How much money does she have?
quiz.mistake: Counts the notes and coins instead of their values

quiz.q: In 555, what is the value of the 5 in the tens place?
quiz.explain: A 5 in the tens place means 5 tens = 50.
quiz.mistake: Thinks every 5 in 555 has the same value

quiz.q: How many hundreds are there in 800?
quiz.explain: 800 = 8 hundreds.
quiz.mistake: Counts tens instead of hundreds

quiz.q: Which number has 6 in the ones place?
quiz.explain: The ones place is the last digit. Only 406 ends in 6.
quiz.mistake: Looks for 6 in any place, not just the ones place

quiz.q: What number is 600 + 5 + 30?
quiz.explain: 600 is 6 hundreds, 30 is 3 tens and 5 is 5 ones. Put them in their places: 635.
quiz.mistake: Writes the digits in the order they are given, not by place

teach.ask: Gappu thinks both 5s in 535 are worth the same. Is he right? Explain to him.
teach.praise: One 5 is 500 and the other is just 5! The place decides the value!
teach.nudge: Where is each 5 sitting? Does that change what it is worth?

learn.hook: Two trains, 845 and 854 passengers. Which one is more crowded? Let's find out!
points: To compare, look at the hundreds first: 512 > 498 because 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds.
If the hundreds are the same, compare the tens. If the tens are also the same, compare the ones.
> means 'greater than' and < means 'less than'. The open side faces the bigger number.
100 more than 345 is 445. 10 less than 345 is 335.

example.q: Arrange 607, 670 and 760 from smallest to biggest.
steps: 607 and 670 both have 6 hundreds. Tens: 0 and 7.

learn.reallife: Comparing prices helps you pick the cheaper cycle, and comparing scores tells you which team won.

games.title: Bigger or smaller?
items: Both have 6 hundreds. 3 tens is more than 0 tens, so 630 > 603.
The hundreds digit goes up by 1: 245 + 100 = 345.
Both have 9 hundreds. 0 tens is less than 9 tens, so 909 < 990.
Same digits in the same places make equal numbers.

quiz.q: Which is greater: 512 or 498?
quiz.explain: Compare hundreds first. 5 hundreds is more than 4 hundreds, so 512 is greater.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the 9s in 498 and thinks it is bigger

quiz.q: Which sign makes this true? 630 ___ 603
quiz.explain: Same hundreds. 3 tens is more than 0 tens, so 630 > 603.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the > and < signs

quiz.q: What is 100 more than 456?
quiz.explain: 100 more adds 1 to the hundreds digit: 456 + 100 = 556.
quiz.mistake: Adds 10 instead of 100

quiz.q: What is 10 less than 382?
quiz.explain: 10 less takes 1 away from the tens digit: 382 − 10 = 372.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 100 instead of 10

quiz.q: Which is the smallest: 415, 451, 514 or 541?
quiz.explain: 415 and 451 have the fewest hundreds (4). Between them, 1 ten is less than 5 tens, so 415 is smallest.
quiz.mistake: Looks only at the last digit

quiz.q: The Delhi train has 845 passengers and the Mumbai train has 854. Which train has more passengers?
quiz.explain: Both have 8 hundreds. 5 tens is more than 4 tens, so 854 is more.
quiz.mistake: Compares the ones digits first

quiz.q: Which list goes from smallest to biggest?
quiz.explain: 230 has 2 hundreds, so it is smallest. 302 has 0 tens and 320 has 2 tens, so 302 comes before 320.
quiz.mistake: Thinks numbers with the same digits are all equal

quiz.q: Using the digits 4, 7 and 2 once each, what is the biggest number you can make?
quiz.explain: Put the biggest digit in the hundreds place, the next in tens, the smallest in ones: 742.
quiz.mistake: Puts the biggest digit in the ones place

teach.ask: Gappu thinks 609 is bigger than 690 because 9 is a big digit. Help him compare!
teach.praise: Same hundreds, so I check the tens! 690 is bigger. Thank you!
teach.nudge: Which place should I look at after the hundreds?

learn.hook: Riya has 3 brothers, and each one gets 2 sweets on Raksha Bandhan. How many sweets does she need?
points: Equal groups have the same number of things in each group.
We can find the total by adding the same number again and again: 3 groups of 2 is 2 + 2 + 2 = 6.
Adding equal groups like this is called multiplication.
We write 3 groups of 2 as 3 × 2 = 6. We say 'three times two is six'.
If the groups are not the same size, they are not equal groups.

example.q: Meena makes 4 rakhis. Each rakhi has 5 beads. How many beads does she use?

learn.reallife: Sweets in a box, eggs in a tray and chairs in rows are all arranged in equal groups.

quiz.q: Riya has 3 brothers. She gives each brother 2 laddoos. How many laddoos does she give?
quiz.explain: 3 groups of 2: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6. That is 3 × 2 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 2 instead of making 3 groups of 2

quiz.q: Which means the same as 4 + 4 + 4?
quiz.explain: There are 3 fours added together. That is 3 groups of 4, or 3 × 4.
quiz.mistake: Uses the number being added for both parts of the multiplication

quiz.q: There are 5 plates with 3 puris on each plate. How many puris are there?
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 and 3 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: There are 2 boxes with 10 rakhis in each box. How many rakhis in all?
quiz.mistake: Counts only one box

quiz.q: Which of these shows EQUAL groups?
quiz.explain: Equal groups have the same number in each group. Only 4, 4 and 4 are all the same.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any set of bags makes equal groups

quiz.q: Arjun says 4 × 2 means 4 groups of 2. What is 4 × 2?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 2 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Aisha's thali has 3 rows of sweets with 6 sweets in each row. Which addition shows the total?
quiz.explain: There are 3 rows, and each row has 6. So we add 6 three times: 6 + 6 + 6.
quiz.mistake: Adds the number of rows instead of the number in each row

quiz.q: Kabir buys 5 rakhis for ₹10 each. How much does he pay?
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 and 10 instead of multiplying

teach.ask: Gappu sees 4 nests with 3 eggs in each. He wants to know how many eggs there are without counting one by one. How?
teach.praise: 4 groups of 3 is 12! Multiplying is so quick!
teach.nudge: Does every nest have the same number? What can I do with that?

learn.hook: A frog that jumps 2 steps each time lands on 2, 4, 6, 8... That's skip counting!
points: Skip counting means jumping by the same number each time.
By 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20 ... These numbers end in 5 or 0.
By 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40 ... These numbers end in 0.
Skip counting is a quick way to count equal groups.

example.q: Count the fingers on 6 hands by skip counting.
steps: Each hand has 5 fingers, so count by 5s.

learn.reallife: Counting pairs of shoes by 2s or ₹10 notes by 10s is skip counting.

quiz.q: Skip count by 2s: 12, 14, 16, ___
quiz.explain: Each jump adds 2. 16 + 2 = 18.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 2

quiz.q: Skip count by 5s: 25, 30, 35, ___
quiz.explain: Each jump adds 5. 35 + 5 = 40.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 or 10 instead of 5

quiz.q: Which number is missing? 4, 8, ___, 16, 20
quiz.explain: The numbers go up by 4 each time. 8 + 4 = 12, and 12 + 4 = 16.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the pattern goes up by 2

quiz.q: How many wheels do 7 bicycles have? Count by 2s.
quiz.explain: Each bicycle has 2 wheels. 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14.
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 and 2

quiz.explain: Each jump adds 10. 50 + 10 = 60.
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 or 1 instead of 10

quiz.q: Which of these numbers will you say when counting by 5s from 5?
quiz.explain: Counting by 5s gives numbers ending in 5 or 0. Only 35 ends in 5 or 0.
quiz.mistake: Does not notice that 5s end in 5 or 0

quiz.q: Joseph counts by 3s: 3, 6, 9, 12. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Each jump adds 3. 12 + 3 = 15.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 3

quiz.q: Harpreet has 4 packets of rakhis with 5 rakhis in each. Count by 5s. How many rakhis?
quiz.explain: 5, 10, 15, 20. Four jumps of 5 make 20.
quiz.mistake: Counts one jump too many

teach.ask: Gappu wants to count 30 grains quickly. He has heard of skip counting. What is it?
teach.praise: Hop, hop, hop by the same number! Counting is faster now!
teach.nudge: Do I jump by a different number each time, or the same number?

learn.hook: Diwali diyas in neat rows look beautiful, and they also help you multiply!
points: An array puts things in rows. 3 rows of 4 is 3 × 4 = 12.
Turn the array around: 4 rows of 3 is also 12. So 3 × 4 = 4 × 3.
× 2 is the same as doubling: 2 × 7 = 14.
× 10 puts a 0 at the end: 6 × 10 = 60.
Learn the tables of 2, 3, 4, 5 and 10 by skip counting.

example.q: Diwali diyas are placed in 4 rows with 6 diyas in each row. How many diyas?

learn.reallife: Seats in a bus, squares on a chocolate bar and windows on a building are all arrays.

quiz.q: There are 3 rows of chairs with 5 chairs in each row. How many chairs?
quiz.mistake: Adds 3 and 5

quiz.q: What is 4 × 3?
quiz.explain: 4 groups of 3: 3, 6, 9, 12.
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 3 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Which is the same as 2 × 6?
quiz.explain: Turning an array around does not change the total. 2 × 6 = 6 × 2 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Thinks changing the order changes the answer

quiz.q: What is 7 × 10?
quiz.explain: 7 tens make 70. Multiplying by 10 puts a 0 at the end.
quiz.mistake: Adds 7 and 10, or puts two zeros

quiz.q: Arjun has 5 packets with 4 pencils in each. How many pencils does he have?
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 and 4

quiz.q: What is double 9?
quiz.explain: Double means 2 times. 9 + 9 = 18.
quiz.mistake: Writes 9 twice side by side

quiz.q: A rangoli has 4 rows of dots with 4 dots in each row. How many dots are there?
quiz.mistake: Adds 4 and 4 only once

quiz.q: Meena knows that 3 × 5 = 15. What is 3 × 6?
quiz.explain: 3 × 6 is 3 groups of 6. That is 1 more in each of the 3 groups than 3 × 5, so add 3: 15 + 3 = 18.
steps: Each of the 3 groups gets 1 more: add 3
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of adding 1 to each of the 3 groups

teach.ask: Gappu arranged his seeds in 2 rows of 5. His friend says 5 rows of 2 is the same amount. Who is right?
teach.praise: 2 × 5 and 5 × 2 are both 10! Turning the rows around keeps the total the same.
teach.nudge: How many seeds are there each way? Is the total the same?

learn.hook: Three friends and twelve laddoos. How can everyone get the same? Let's share fairly!
points: Sharing fairly means everyone gets the same amount.
To share, give one to each person, again and again, until none are left.
12 laddoos shared by 3 friends: each friend gets 4.
Sometimes some are left over. Leftovers cannot be shared equally.
Check your sharing by multiplying: 3 friends × 4 laddoos = 12.

example.q: Kabir shares 15 marbles equally among 5 friends. How many marbles does each friend get?
steps: Give 1 marble to each friend again and again.

learn.reallife: Sharing a pack of biscuits with your cousins or dividing team players for a cricket match needs equal sharing.

games.title: Fair or not?
items: 8 apples shared by 2 children is 4 each.
Fair sharing means the oldest child gets more.
Fair means everyone gets the same amount.
9 bananas can be shared equally by 2 children with none left over.
Each gets 4 and 1 banana is left over.
16 crayons shared by 4 children is 4 each.
If 3 friends get 5 sweets each, there were 15 sweets.

quiz.q: Riya shares 12 laddoos equally among 3 friends. How many laddoos does each friend get?
quiz.explain: 12 shared into 3 equal groups gives 4 in each group. Check: 3 × 4 = 12.
steps: Give one to each friend: 3 gone
quiz.mistake: Takes away 3 from 12 instead of sharing

quiz.q: Arjun shares 10 kites equally between his 2 cousins. How many kites does each cousin get?
quiz.explain: 10 shared by 2 gives 5 each. 5 + 5 = 10.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 2 instead of sharing

quiz.q: 20 rotis are shared equally by 4 people. How many rotis does each person get?
quiz.explain: 20 shared into 4 equal groups gives 5 each. Check: 4 × 5 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 4 instead of sharing

quiz.q: Meena shares 7 toffees equally between 2 friends. How many toffees are left over?
quiz.explain: Each friend gets 3 toffees. 3 + 3 = 6, so 7 − 6 = 1 is left over.
quiz.mistake: Gives the number each friend gets, not the leftover

quiz.q: Which is a FAIR share of 6 bananas for 2 children?
quiz.explain: Fair means the same amount. 3 and 3 are equal, and 3 + 3 = 6.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any split that adds up to 6 is fair

quiz.q: Kabir shares 18 pencils equally among 6 friends. How many pencils does each friend get?
quiz.explain: 18 shared into 6 equal groups gives 3 each. Check: 6 × 3 = 18.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 6 instead of sharing

quiz.q: 5 friends each got 4 samosas. How many samosas were shared?
quiz.mistake: Adds 5 and 4 instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Aisha shares 9 stickers equally among her 3 friends. How many stickers does each friend get?
quiz.explain: 9 shared into 3 equal groups gives 3 each. 3 + 3 + 3 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Takes away 3 from 9 instead of sharing

teach.ask: Gappu and his 2 friends found 9 worms. Gappu wants to keep 5! What is a fair way to share them?
teach.praise: 3 worms each, the same for everyone. That is fair!
teach.nudge: If I take 5, will everyone get the same? How many should each friend get?

learn.hook: Can you cut a roti so that you and your sister get exactly the same? That's a half!
points: When one whole is cut into 2 equal parts, each part is a half.
We write one half as 1/2.
The two parts must be the same size. Unequal parts are not halves.
2 halves make 1 whole.
Half of a group: half of 10 laddoos is 5, because 10 shared by 2 is 5.

example.q: Joseph cuts a roti into 2 equal pieces and eats one piece. What part of the roti did he eat?
steps: The roti is cut into 2 equal parts.
He ate 1 of the 2 equal parts.
1 out of 2 equal parts is one half.

learn.reallife: Half a glass of milk, half an hour of play and half a cricket field are all halves around us.

games.title: Halves or not?
items: A roti cut into 2 equal parts
A paper folded exactly in the middle
A chocolate broken into a big piece and a small piece
An apple cut into 3 equal parts
A square cut corner to corner into 2 equal triangles
A cake cut into 2 parts, one big and one small

quiz.q: A laddoo is cut into 2 equal parts. What is each part called?
quiz.explain: When a whole is cut into 2 equal parts, each part is one half.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up half (2 equal parts) and quarter (4 equal parts)

quiz.q: Which fraction means 'one half'?
quiz.explain: 1/2 means 1 out of 2 equal parts.
quiz.mistake: Writes the numbers the wrong way up

quiz.q: What is half of 12 bananas?
quiz.explain: Half means share into 2 equal groups. 12 shared by 2 is 6. 6 + 6 = 12.
quiz.mistake: Doubles the number instead of halving it

quiz.q: How many halves make 1 whole?
quiz.explain: A whole cut into halves has 2 equal parts. 2 halves make 1 whole.
quiz.mistake: Thinks one half is already a whole

quiz.q: Arjun breaks a chocolate into a big piece and a small piece. Are the pieces halves?
options: No, the pieces are not equal
quiz.explain: Halves must be 2 EQUAL parts. A big piece and a small piece are not equal.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any 2 pieces are halves

quiz.q: Riya has 16 bangles. She gives half of them to her sister. How many bangles does she give?
quiz.explain: Half of 16 is 16 shared by 2. 8 + 8 = 16, so half is 8.
quiz.mistake: Finds a quarter instead of a half

quiz.q: Kabir and Harpreet share ₹20 equally. How much does each get?
quiz.explain: Sharing equally by 2 means each gets half. Half of ₹20 is ₹10. 10 + 10 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Doubles instead of halving

quiz.q: Meena ate half of a pizza. Kabir ate the other half. How much pizza did they eat in all?
quiz.explain: Two halves make one whole. So they ate the whole pizza.
quiz.mistake: Thinks two halves make two wholes

teach.ask: Gappu cut his chapati into 2 pieces, one big and one tiny. He says each is a half. Is he right?
teach.praise: Halves must be the same size! I will cut it again, fairly this time.
teach.nudge: Are my two pieces the same size? What must be true for halves?

learn.hook: Cut a watermelon into 4 equal slices and share with your family. Each slice is a quarter!
points: When one whole is cut into 4 equal parts, each part is a quarter. We write it as 1/4.
4 quarters make 1 whole. 2 quarters make a half.
3 out of 4 equal parts is three quarters, written 3/4.
A quarter of 8 laddoos is 2, because 8 shared by 4 is 2.
A quarter is smaller than a half of the same thing.

example.q: A watermelon is cut into 4 equal slices. Riya eats 1 slice and Arjun eats 2 slices. What part did they eat together?

learn.reallife: A quarter of an hour, a quarter of a cake and a quarter of a pizza are all around us.

games.title: Quarter quiz
items: A quarter of a roti is bigger than half of the same roti.
Cutting into 4 parts makes smaller pieces than cutting into 2.
2 out of 4 equal parts is the same as 1 out of 2.
All 4 equal parts together make the whole.
Any 4 pieces of a roti are quarters.
The 4 pieces must be equal to be quarters.
Three quarters means 3 out of 4 equal parts.

quiz.q: A roti is cut into 4 equal pieces. What is one piece called?
quiz.explain: 1 out of 4 equal parts is a quarter.
quiz.mistake: Calls any piece a half

quiz.q: How many quarters make one whole?
quiz.explain: A whole cut into quarters has 4 equal parts. All 4 make the whole.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up quarters with halves

quiz.q: What is a quarter of 8 laddoos?
quiz.explain: A quarter means share into 4 equal groups. 8 shared by 4 is 2.
quiz.mistake: Finds half instead of a quarter

quiz.q: A cake is cut into 4 equal parts and 3 parts are eaten. What fraction of the cake is eaten?
quiz.explain: 3 out of 4 equal parts are eaten. That is three quarters, 3/4.
quiz.mistake: Writes the part that is left, or turns the fraction upside down

quiz.q: Which is bigger: half of a roti, or a quarter of the same roti?
quiz.explain: Cutting into 2 parts gives bigger pieces than cutting into 4. So a half is bigger.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 4 is bigger than 2, so a quarter must be bigger

quiz.q: How many quarters make a half?
quiz.explain: 2 quarters out of 4 is the same as 1 half out of 2.
quiz.mistake: Thinks it takes 4 quarters to make a half

quiz.q: Aisha has 20 marbles. She gives a quarter of them to Joseph. How many marbles does Joseph get?
quiz.explain: A quarter of 20 is 20 shared by 4. 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 20, so it is 5.
quiz.mistake: Finds half instead of a quarter

quiz.q: A pizza has 4 equal slices. Kabir eats 1 slice. What part of the pizza is left?
quiz.explain: 4 − 1 = 3 slices are left. 3 out of 4 equal slices is three quarters.
quiz.mistake: Names the part eaten instead of the part left

teach.ask: Gappu cut a mango into 4 equal pieces and gave one to his friend. What part did his friend get?
teach.praise: One out of four equal pieces is a quarter! Thank you!
teach.nudge: How many equal pieces were there? What do we call one of them?

learn.hook: A school has hundreds of boys and hundreds of girls. How many children in all? Let's add big numbers!
points: Write the numbers one below the other: ones under ones, tens under tens, hundreds under hundreds.
Add the ones first, then the tens, then the hundreds.
324 + 152: ones 4 + 2 = 6, tens 2 + 5 = 7, hundreds 3 + 1 = 4. The answer is 476.
Adding hundreds is easy: 300 + 400 = 700, just like 3 + 4 = 7.

example.q: A school has 213 boys and 245 girls. How many children are there?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers add up how many things they sold in a day, and railways add up passengers on each train.

quiz.q: What is 231 + 425?
quiz.explain: Ones 1 + 5 = 6, tens 3 + 2 = 5, hundreds 2 + 4 = 6. So 656.
quiz.mistake: Makes a slip when adding one of the places

quiz.q: A train has 342 people in the front coaches and 215 in the back coaches. How many people are on the train?
quiz.explain: Ones 2 + 5 = 7, tens 4 + 1 = 5, hundreds 3 + 2 = 5. So 557.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of adding

quiz.q: What is 600 + 300?
quiz.explain: 6 hundreds + 3 hundreds = 9 hundreds = 900.
quiz.mistake: Adds an extra zero

quiz.q: Riya scored 123 points in a game and Arjun scored 104 points. What is their total score?
quiz.explain: Ones 3 + 4 = 7, tens 2 + 0 = 2, hundreds 1 + 1 = 2. So 227.
quiz.mistake: Makes a slip in the tens place

quiz.q: In the column method, which place do we add first?
quiz.explain: We start with the ones. If they make a new ten, we can carry it to the tens.
quiz.mistake: Starts from the left like reading

quiz.q: A shop sold 410 diyas on Monday and 380 diyas on Tuesday. How many diyas were sold?
quiz.explain: Ones 0 + 0 = 0, tens 1 + 8 = 9, hundreds 4 + 3 = 7. So 790.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts instead of adding

quiz.q: Kabir adds 500 + 40 + 7 + 200. What does he get?
quiz.explain: Hundreds: 500 + 200 = 700. Tens: 40. Ones: 7. So 747.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the last 200

quiz.q: Aisha read 125 pages and then 63 more pages. How many pages did she read?
quiz.explain: Line up the places. Ones 5 + 3 = 8, tens 2 + 6 = 8, hundreds 1. So 188.
quiz.mistake: Writes 63 under the hundreds and tens instead of the tens and ones

teach.ask: Gappu wants to add 312 and 145, but he started adding from the left and got muddled. How should he do it?
teach.praise: Line up the places and start with the ones! 457! Hooray!
teach.nudge: Which place should I start with? And how should I write the numbers?

learn.hook: What if the ones add up to more than 9? Time to carry a ten to its new house!
points: If the ones add up to 10 or more, make 1 ten and carry it to the tens place.
If the tens add up to 10 or more, make 1 hundred and carry it to the hundreds place.
256 + 137: ones 6 + 7 = 13, write 3 and carry 1. Tens 5 + 3 + 1 = 9. Hundreds 2 + 1 = 3. Answer 393.
Always remember to add the number you carried!

example.q: Meena collected 178 shells and Joseph collected 145 shells. How many shells in all?

learn.reallife: When you add up runs scored in two innings, you often need to carry.

games.title: Did they carry right?
items: When ones add up to 13, we write 3 and carry 1 ten.
We never need to carry in the tens place.
If the tens add up to 10 or more, we carry 1 hundred.

quiz.q: What is 268 + 125?
quiz.explain: 8 + 5 = 13: write 3, carry 1. Tens 6 + 2 + 1 = 9. Hundreds 2 + 1 = 3. So 393.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the carried 1

quiz.q: What is 147 + 38?
quiz.explain: 7 + 8 = 15: write 5, carry 1. Tens 4 + 3 + 1 = 8. Hundreds 1. So 185.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the carried 1

quiz.q: A library has 365 storybooks and 248 comics. How many books are there in all?
quiz.explain: Ones 5 + 8 = 13, carry 1. Tens 6 + 4 + 1 = 11, carry 1. Hundreds 3 + 2 + 1 = 6. So 613.
quiz.mistake: Forgets one of the carries

quiz.q: In 459 + 236, the ones are 9 + 6 = 15. What do we do next?
quiz.explain: 15 is 1 ten and 5 ones. The 5 stays in the ones place and the 1 ten moves to the tens place.
quiz.mistake: Writes both digits of 15 in the ones place

quiz.q: Harpreet's family drove 189 km on day 1 and 211 km on day 2. How far did they drive in all?
quiz.explain: Ones 9 + 1 = 10, carry 1. Tens 8 + 1 + 1 = 10, carry 1. Hundreds 1 + 2 + 1 = 4. So 400 km.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry when a place adds up to exactly 10

quiz.q: Riya had ₹475. She got ₹125 on Diwali. How much money does she have now?
quiz.explain: Ones 5 + 5 = 10, carry 1. Tens 7 + 2 + 1 = 10, carry 1. Hundreds 4 + 1 + 1 = 6. So ₹600.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to carry from the ones

quiz.q: What is 99 + 99?
quiz.explain: Ones 9 + 9 = 18, carry 1. Tens 9 + 9 + 1 = 19, carry 1. Hundreds 1. So 198.
quiz.mistake: Forgets to add the carried 1 in the tens

quiz.q: A tea stall sold 236 cups of tea in the morning and 186 in the evening. How many cups in all?
quiz.explain: Ones 6 + 6 = 12, carry 1. Tens 3 + 8 + 1 = 12, carry 1. Hundreds 2 + 1 + 1 = 4. So 422.
quiz.mistake: Forgets one of the carries

teach.ask: Gappu added 47 + 28 and wrote 615! What went wrong? Explain carrying to him.
teach.praise: 15 ones is 1 ten and 5 ones! So 47 + 28 = 75. I get it now!
teach.nudge: What should I do when the ones add up to more than 9?

learn.hook: How do you take 7 away from 2? Borrow from the tens house next door!
points: Line up the places and subtract the ones first.
If the top ones digit is smaller, break 1 ten into 10 ones. This is called borrowing or regrouping.
352 − 127: 2 − 7 is not possible, so break a ten: 12 − 7 = 5. Tens: 4 − 2 = 2. Hundreds: 3 − 1 = 2. Answer 225.
If the top tens digit is too small, break 1 hundred into 10 tens.
Check by adding: 225 + 127 = 352.

example.q: A shop had 430 kites and sold 185. How many kites are left?
steps: Ones: 0 − 5 is not possible. Break a ten: 10 − 5 = 5. Now 2 tens are left.
Tens: 2 − 8 is not possible. Break a hundred: 12 − 8 = 4. Now 3 hundreds are left.

learn.reallife: Finding how many pages are left to read or how much money is left after shopping uses subtraction.

quiz.q: What is 463 − 128?
quiz.explain: 3 − 8 is not possible, so break a ten: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. Hundreds: 4 − 1 = 3. So 335.
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller digit from the bigger one (8 − 3) instead of borrowing

quiz.q: A train had 275 passengers. 132 got off at Jaipur. How many passengers are on the train now?
quiz.explain: Ones 5 − 2 = 3, tens 7 − 3 = 4, hundreds 2 − 1 = 1. So 143.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of subtracting

quiz.q: A school has 520 children. 248 of them are girls. How many are boys?
quiz.explain: Ones: break a ten, 10 − 8 = 2. Tens: break a hundred, 11 − 4 = 7. Hundreds: 4 − 2 = 2. So 272.
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller digit from the bigger one in each place instead of borrowing

quiz.q: What is 400 − 1?
quiz.explain: 1 less than 400 is 399. Counting back: 401, 400, 399.
quiz.mistake: Takes away from the hundreds instead of the ones

quiz.q: Kabir had ₹350. He spent ₹175. How much money is left?
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller digit from the bigger one instead of borrowing

quiz.q: To check that 610 − 245 = 365, which addition should you do?
quiz.explain: Add the answer to the number taken away. 365 + 245 = 610, so the answer is right.
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers from the question

quiz.q: In 342 − 118, the ones are 2 − 8. What should we do first?
quiz.explain: 2 is smaller than 8, so we break 1 ten from the tens place. Now we have 12 ones, and 12 − 8 = 4.
quiz.mistake: Swaps the digits and does 8 − 2

quiz.q: Meena's storybook has 300 pages. She has read 126 pages. How many pages are left?
quiz.explain: 300 − 126: break a hundred into tens and a ten into ones. Ones 10 − 6 = 4, tens 9 − 2 = 7, hundreds 2 − 1 = 1. So 174.
quiz.mistake: Takes the smaller digit from the bigger one in each place

teach.ask: Gappu is doing 52 − 27. He says '2 − 7? I'll just do 7 − 2!' Help him do it the right way.
teach.praise: Break a ten, then 12 − 7 = 5. 52 − 27 = 25! I won't flip the digits again.
teach.nudge: If the top digit is smaller, where can I get more ones from?

learn.hook: 2, 4, 6, 8... who do we appreciate? Number patterns, of course!
points: A pattern follows a rule again and again.
Some patterns grow by adding: 2, 4, 6, 8 (add 2 each time).
Some patterns get smaller by taking away: 50, 45, 40 (take away 5 each time).
Find the rule by looking at how each number changes to the next.
Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. Odd numbers end in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9. They take turns: even, odd, even, odd.

example.q: What comes next: 3, 7, 11, 15, ___?

learn.reallife: House numbers on one side of a street often go 2, 4, 6, 8 and on the other side 1, 3, 5, 7.

quiz.q: What comes next? 5, 10, 15, 20, ___
quiz.explain: The rule is 'add 5'. 20 + 5 = 25.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 5

quiz.q: What is the rule? 30, 27, 24, 21
quiz.explain: Each number is 3 less than the one before: 30 − 3 = 27, 27 − 3 = 24.
quiz.mistake: Sees a jump of 3 but misses that the numbers are getting smaller

quiz.q: Find the missing number: 6, 12, ___, 24, 30
quiz.explain: The rule is 'add 6'. 12 + 6 = 18, and 18 + 6 = 24.
quiz.mistake: Uses a jump of 2 or 4 instead of 6

quiz.q: What comes next? 1, 4, 7, 10, ___
quiz.explain: The rule is 'add 3'. 10 + 3 = 13.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 or 2 instead of 3

quiz.q: Which number is EVEN?
quiz.explain: Even numbers end in 0, 2, 4, 6 or 8. 58 ends in 8.
quiz.mistake: Looks at the tens digit instead of the ones digit

quiz.q: At the party, Riya puts 2 balloons on the first chair, 4 on the second and 6 on the third. How many on the fourth chair?
quiz.explain: The rule is 'add 2'. 6 + 2 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 2

quiz.q: What comes next? 50, 40, 30, ___
quiz.explain: The rule is 'take away 10'. 30 − 10 = 20.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the pattern goes up instead of down

quiz.q: Arjun's pattern is 2, 4, 8, 16, ___. Each number is double the one before. What comes next?
quiz.explain: Double 16 is 16 + 16 = 32.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 each time instead of doubling

teach.ask: Gappu sees 4, 8, 12, 16 on the party board. How can he find the next number?
teach.praise: Add 4 each time! The next number is 20!
teach.nudge: How does each number change to the next one?

learn.hook: Party flags, bangles and rangoli all have patterns. Can you guess what comes next?
points: A repeating pattern has a part that comes again and again: 🔴🔵🔴🔵.
The part that repeats is called the core. In red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, the core is red, blue, blue.
A growing pattern gets bigger at each step: 1 dot, 2 dots, 3 dots.
To find what comes next, find the core or the rule first.

example.q: Party flags go: green, yellow, yellow, green, yellow, yellow, ___. What comes next?
steps: The core is green, yellow, yellow.
After the second yellow, the core starts again.

learn.reallife: Borders of saris, bead necklaces and paper chains for parties all show patterns.

items.text: A, B, B, A, B, B, ___

games.title: Pattern detective
items: Red, blue, red, blue is a repeating pattern.
Red, blue comes again and again.
A growing pattern gets bigger at each step.
In red, white, red, white ..., the 6th bead is white.
Red is in places 1, 3, 5. White is in places 2, 4, 6.
Circle, square, circle, square ...: the 5th shape is a square.

quiz.q: What comes next? 🔴🟢🔴🟢🔴___
quiz.explain: The core is 🔴🟢. After 🔴 comes 🟢.
quiz.mistake: Repeats the last colour instead of following the core

quiz.q: Bangles go: red, red, gold, red, red, gold. What is the core of this pattern?
quiz.explain: The part that repeats is red, red, gold.
quiz.mistake: Misses one of the reds in the core

quiz.q: Rangoli dots go: 1 dot, 3 dots, 5 dots, 7 dots. How many dots come next?
quiz.explain: Each step adds 2 dots. 7 + 2 = 9.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 instead of 2

quiz.q: A paper chain goes pink, blue, pink, blue ... What colour is the 8th ring?
quiz.explain: Pink is in places 1, 3, 5, 7. Blue is in places 2, 4, 6, 8. So the 8th ring is blue.
quiz.mistake: Loses count of the places

quiz.q: Which of these is a GROWING pattern?
quiz.explain: In ⭐, ⭐⭐, ⭐⭐⭐ each step has one more star, so it grows.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up repeating patterns with growing patterns

quiz.q: Kabir sets plates: big, small, small, big, small, small, big, ___. What comes next?
quiz.explain: The core is big, small, small. After 'big' comes 'small'.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the pattern just takes turns, big then small then big

quiz.q: Tiles: step 1 has 2 tiles, step 2 has 4 tiles, step 3 has 6 tiles. How many tiles in step 4?
quiz.explain: Each step adds 2 tiles. 6 + 2 = 8.
quiz.mistake: Adds 1 tile instead of 2

quiz.q: A border goes triangle, circle, square, triangle, circle, square ... Which shape is 7th?
quiz.explain: The core has 3 shapes. Places 1, 4 and 7 are triangles.
quiz.mistake: Counts the places wrongly

teach.ask: Gappu made a necklace: red bead, yellow bead, yellow bead, red bead, yellow bead... What bead comes next and how do you know?
teach.praise: Red, yellow, yellow keeps repeating, so yellow comes next! My necklace looks lovely.
teach.nudge: Which part of my necklace keeps coming again?

learn.hook: Fold a paper butterfly down the middle. Both wings match perfectly. That's symmetry!
points: A shape is symmetrical if one half is a mirror image of the other half.
The fold line that makes two matching halves is called the line of symmetry.
Letters like A, H, M, O, T, U, V, W, X and Y have matching halves when folded along a standing line down the middle.
Some shapes have more than one line of symmetry. A square has 4. A circle has many.
Rangoli and kolam designs are often symmetrical.

example.q: How many lines of symmetry does a long rectangle, like a door, have?
steps: Fold it along a standing line down the middle: the halves match.
Fold it along a sleeping line across the middle: the halves match.
Fold it corner to corner: the halves do NOT match.

learn.reallife: Butterflies, leaves, diyas, the Taj Mahal and many rangoli designs are symmetrical.

games.title: Mirror, mirror
items: A square has 4 lines of symmetry.
2 folds through the middle of the sides and 2 folds corner to corner.
No fold makes the two halves of F match.
A circle has many lines of symmetry.
Any fold through the centre makes two matching halves.
A long rectangle, like a door, has 4 lines of symmetry.
It has only 2. Corner-to-corner folds do not match.
The two halves of a symmetrical shape match exactly.

quiz.q: What do we call the fold line that splits a shape into two matching halves?
quiz.explain: A line of symmetry divides a shape into two halves that are mirror images.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the line of symmetry with the edge of the shape

quiz.q: Which letter is symmetrical?
quiz.explain: Fold H down the middle and both halves match. F, G and R do not have matching halves.
quiz.mistake: Picks a letter without trying to fold it in the mind

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a square have?
quiz.explain: A square can be folded top to bottom, side to side and along both corner-to-corner lines. That makes 4.
quiz.mistake: Forgets the corner-to-corner folds

quiz.q: Riya folds a paper heart down the middle and the two halves match. The heart is ___.
quiz.explain: When two halves match exactly after folding, the shape is symmetrical.
quiz.mistake: Does not connect matching halves with symmetry

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT symmetrical?
quiz.explain: J has a hook on one side only, so no fold makes its halves match.
quiz.mistake: Misses the word NOT in the question

quiz.q: How many lines of symmetry does a long rectangle, like a door, have?
quiz.explain: Folding down the middle and across the middle both work. Corner-to-corner folds do not.
steps: Corner to corner: does not match
quiz.mistake: Thinks a rectangle has 4 lines like a square

quiz.q: Aisha drew half of a rangoli flower. To make it symmetrical, the other half must be ___.
options: a mirror copy of the first half
quiz.explain: In a symmetrical design, one half is a mirror image of the other.
quiz.mistake: Thinks symmetry means just filling the space

quiz.q: Which word is made ONLY of letters that match when folded down the middle?
quiz.explain: T, O, M and A all match when folded down the middle. MANGO has N and G, CAKE has C, K and E, PIZZA has P and Z. These do not.
quiz.mistake: Checks only some of the letters

teach.ask: Gappu found a butterfly and a leaf. His friend says they are symmetrical. What does that mean?
teach.praise: Fold it in the middle and both halves match! Butterflies are symmetrical!
teach.nudge: What happens to the two halves when I fold it down the middle?

learn.hook: A bucket or a cup: which one would you use to fill a bathtub? Let's compare how much things hold!
points: Capacity is how much a container can hold.
We can compare by filling one container and pouring it into another.
We can measure with small cups or glasses: a jug may hold 6 glasses of water.
Litre (L) is the standard unit for liquids like milk, water and oil.
Small amounts are measured in millilitres (mL). 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.

example.q: A bucket holds 10 mugs of water. A pot holds 4 mugs. How many more mugs does the bucket hold?

learn.reallife: Milk comes in 1 litre and half-litre packets, and water bottles are often 1 litre.

games.title: Less or more than a litre?
Little to large
games.prompt: Holds the least to holds the most

quiz.q: Which of these holds the MOST water?
quiz.explain: A bucket is much bigger inside than a cup, spoon or glass, so it holds the most.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up most and least

quiz.q: Which unit do we use to measure milk?
quiz.explain: Liquids like milk are measured in litres.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the unit for weight with the unit for liquids

quiz.q: One jug of water fills 5 glasses. How many glasses do 2 jugs fill?
quiz.explain: 2 jugs fill 5 + 5 = 10 glasses.
quiz.mistake: Adds 2 and 5

quiz.q: How many millilitres are there in 1 litre?
quiz.explain: 1 litre = 1000 millilitres.
quiz.mistake: Thinks 1 litre is 100 millilitres

quiz.q: Riya's bottle holds 2 litres of water. She drinks 1 litre. How much water is left?
quiz.explain: 2 litres − 1 litre = 1 litre.
quiz.mistake: Adds instead of taking away
